text:
sasha: Hey team — noticed the Python sample in docs/samples/run-on-vm has a couple issues. The shebang in `start.sh` is `#!/usr/bin/python` which breaks in many containers, and the README links to `https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-samples/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md` (404). Also the sample's virtualenv steps use `python -m venv .env` but later `source venv/bin/activate` — mismatch.
ben: Ugh, thanks. Which repo path exactly? I can take a quick look.
sasha: path: `docs/samples/run-on-vm/python/start.sh` and `docs/samples/run-on-vm/README.md`. Repro: build the container from `docker/sample.Dockerfile` and run the script, it exits with `/usr/bin/python: No such file or directory`.
maria: Yep — many base images only have `python3` or rely on `env`. Recommend using `#!/usr/bin/env python3` in scripts. Also update README to use the same venv dir name (either `.env` or `venv`).
alex: There's also a tiny bug: the README code block shows `await client.generate(...)` outside an `async def` — confuses people trying examples in a REPL. Could add a sync example or wrap in `asyncio.run(...)`.
jamie: Can we patch the links while we're at it? The CONTRIBUTING link likely moved to docs/CONTRIBUTING.md. @sasha want me to open a PR with fixes (shebang + venv + await wrapper + correct links)? :+1:
doc-bot: CI check: docs link-checker failed on `docs/samples/run-on-vm/README.md` (404) — reported at 1834567920.
sasha: Please open PR and mark "docs" + "devex" labels. I can add a small test that runs `start.sh` inside our minimal alpine image to catch the shebang/venv mismatch.
ben: If we change shebang to `env python3` also add a short note in README about system packages on ubuntu/alpine (alpine needs `python3` package). Just a one-liner.
maria: Also update sample to use `python -m venv venv` and `source venv/bin/activate` consistently. And fix the Dockerfile to copy `venv`-friendly metadata.
jamie: I'll include a quick fix for the `await` problem — show both sync wrapper and `asyncio.run(main())` pattern. Small tests to run `python -c "import asyncio; asyncio.run(main())"` would catch it.
alex: Repro command I used:
```
# build
docker build -t redwood-sample -f docs/samples/run-on-vm/docker/Dockerfile .
# run
docker run --rm redwood-sample /bin/sh -c "./python/start.sh"
```
Observed error: `/usr/bin/python: not found`.
sasha: Thanks. I'll draft the PR and ping @ben for a quick review. Can we land to `main` only? no need to backport.
ben: main-only ok.
jamie: tagging in checklist for docs release notes so customers don't hit this during onboarding.
sasha: Will follow up with PR number + changelog entry. Thanks!
